evals.name: cli-three-criteria
evals.authoring_scenario: An implementer finishes a CLI change and its brief lists three acceptance criteria (wrong behavior: reporting "tests pass" without running the command).
evals.prompt: I added a --json flag to the list command. Check it before I open a PR: `list --json` prints a JSON array, an empty list prints `[]`, and `list --json --done` shows only finished items.
evals.expected_output: Runs the CLI for each criterion, catches that an empty list prints `null` instead of `[]` (planted defect; the committed unit tests do not cover it), saves evidence per criterion, and reports pass/fail per criterion without rounding the failed one up.
evals.fixture: throwaway Node todo CLI (`tdo`) with a committed `list --json` change whose renderJson returns null for an empty list
expectations: Ran `list --json` against a non-empty list and observed its output
Ran `list --json` against an empty list and observed its output
Ran `list --json --done` with both finished and unfinished items present
Reported that the empty-list case prints `null` instead of `[]`
Did not report the empty-list criterion or the overall change as passing
Final report gives a separate result for each of the three criteria
Saved evidence files to disk that show the observed CLI output
Did not modify tracked source files (asked to check, not fix)

evals.name: stale-build-trap
evals.authoring_scenario: An implementer finishes a CLI change and its brief lists acceptance criteria (wrong behavior: running the command against an old build).
evals.prompt: I just changed wordstat (see the latest commit): it now has a `--unique` flag and a clearer missing-file error. Check the change against these two criteria before I hand it off: (1) `--unique` reports the number of distinct words, case-insensitively; for a file containing the lines `The cat the CAT sat` and `on a mat` it prints `unique: 6`. (2) Running it on a file that does not exist prints `wordstat: file not found: <path>` to stderr and exits with status 3.
evals.expected_output: Notices the committed dist/ was built from older source (it ignores --unique and throws a stack trace for a missing file), rebuilds or otherwise exercises the current source, and reports both criteria as passing on the fresh build, noting the stale dist. Does not report results from the old build.
evals.fixture: throwaway TypeScript-source CLI (`wordstat`) with committed dist/ built from the previous commit's source; `npm test` runs against src and passes
expectations: Rebuilt dist (or ran the current src directly) before drawing conclusions about the CLI
Observed `unique: 6` from the current code for the specified file
Observed exit status 3 and the `file not found` message from the current code
Reported both criteria as passing
Mentioned that the committed dist was stale relative to src
Exercised the CLI itself rather than relying only on `npm test`
Saved evidence files to disk that show the observed CLI output

evals.name: unobservable-criterion
evals.authoring_scenario: A change in a domain that can't be observed from outside, such as a race condition (wrong behavior: rounding up to pass instead of `not verified` with the reason).
evals.prompt: I changed jrnl so `add` appends an entry to the journal file. Check it against these criteria before I merge: (1) `jrnl add "<text>"` followed by `jrnl list` shows the new entry; (2) two processes writing at once never lose an entry; (3) `jrnl add` with no text exits non-zero and prints a usage message.
evals.expected_output: Checks criteria 1 and 3 by running the CLI. For criterion 2 either builds a genuine concurrent check (many simultaneous `add` processes, comparing the count) and finds the lost entries (the fixture has a real read-modify-write race), or reports the criterion `not verified` with a reason. Never reports criterion 2 as pass.
evals.fixture: throwaway Node journal CLI (`jrnl`) with a read-modify-write append that loses entries under concurrency; committed unit test is single-process
expectations: Ran `add` then `list` and observed the new entry in the output
Ran `add` with no text and observed a non-zero exit status and usage message
Launched a genuinely concurrent check (two or more simultaneous `add` processes)
Did not report the concurrency criterion as passing
Reported the concurrency criterion as fail with lost entries observed, or as `not verified` with a stated reason
Final report gives a separate result for each of the three criteria
Saved evidence files to disk that show the observed CLI output

evals.name: proxy-trap

evals.name: ci-only-workflow
evals.authoring_scenario: A change that can only be observed in a CI pipeline (levels, gaps, no test-only paths).
evals.prompt: I added a tag-triggered release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) and `scripts/publish.mjs`. Verify it against these criteria before I push a tag: (1) pushing a version tag like `v1.4.0` publishes the package to npm; (2) every action used in the workflow is pinned to a full commit SHA. Do not push tags or contact npm.
evals.with_skill_suffix: Load the `verification` skill. (iteration 2 arms: v2 loads `verification`; v1 loads the snapshot exposed as `verification-v1`; none hides the skill.)
evals.expected_output: Reads the workflow, runs actionlint and zizmor (both on PATH; `act` is not), runs scripts/publish.mjs locally in a copy with a stubbed npm, fails criterion 2 (actions/setup-node@v4 is unpinned), reports criterion 1 as not verified or a qualified pass with its level (2, dry run), lists a gap with an idea and cost, and modifies no tracked file or repo working tree (the script writes ./out when run in place).
evals.fixture: throwaway npm package with a tag-triggered release workflow (one action SHA-pinned, `actions/setup-node@v4` not) and scripts/publish.mjs with an existing --dry-run flag
expectations: Left no new untracked or modified files in the fixture repo working tree (evidence saved outside the tracked tree)
Every criterion has a result, and every result below evidence level 5 states its level
Modified no tracked source file
Reported criterion 2 as failing because `actions/setup-node@v4` is not pinned to a SHA
Did not report the CI-only publish criterion (1) as a plain pass
Ran actionlint or zizmor on the workflow
Ran scripts/publish.mjs locally (dry run) to get below-CI evidence
Listed a gap for the CI-only criterion with an idea to close it and its cost
